decision_table.name: Determine_CT_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file CT state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in CT (office, employees, property)

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - CT filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
CT filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
Reference: CT Department of Revenue Services, Corporation Business Tax Return Form CT-1120 Reference: CT General Statutes § 12-214 (Corporate tax imposed)

CT filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair). Connecticut threshold: $500,000 in gross receipts (no transaction count requirement).
This is higher than the typical $100,000 threshold used by many states, reflecting Connecticut's business-friendly approach to smaller out-of-state corporations.
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: CT DRS Economic Nexus Guidance
No CT nexus - no filing requirement. Any estimated payments would be refunded.

decision_table.name: Calculate_CT_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate CT state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
CT state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
Additions to federal taxable income include: - Interest on U.S. government obligations (federally tax-exempt, CT taxable) - IRC Section 199A qualified business income deduction (CT addback) - Bonus depreciation (CT decouples from federal bonus depreciation) - Other items per CT Form CT-1120 Schedule I
Subtractions from federal taxable income include: - Interest on CT state and municipal bonds - CT net operating loss deduction - Dividend deduction for certain subsidiary corporations - Other items per CT Form CT-1120 Schedule J
Reference: CT Form CT-1120 Instructions (Schedules I and J) Reference: CT General Statutes § 12-217 (Computation of tax) Reference: CT DRS Special Notice 2018(5) - Federal Tax Reform
No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.

decision_table.name: Calculate_CT_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate CT state corporate income tax. Applies CT 7.5% flat tax rate to apportioned and adjusted taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
CT state corporate income tax calculation:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to CT: × [Single-sales apportionment %] 3. State additions: + [Additions per Schedule I] 4. State subtractions: - [Subtractions per Schedule J] 5. CT taxable income: = [Result] 6. CT tax rate: × 7.5% 7. CT income tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. CT credits: - [Credits] 9. CT tax liability: = [Final tax]
Connecticut uses a flat 7.5% tax rate on all corporate income. This rate has been stable since 2018.
Reference: CT Form CT-1120 Corporation Business Tax Return Reference: CT General Statutes § 12-214 (Tax imposed - 7.5% rate) Reference: CT DRS Form CT-1120 Instructions
No CT nexus - no tax liability. Any estimated payments are refunded.

No CT taxable income - no tax liability. CT NOL rules may apply (can carry forward losses to future years).
Reference: CT General Statutes § 12-217(a)(2) (NOL carryforward)
